President Donald Trump drew attention after telling reporters that the United States has the “best poverty numbers ever,” adding that there is less poverty now than at any point in the country’s history. His comments appear to reference newly released Census Bureau data showing that the official U.S. poverty rate fell from 10.6% in 2024 to 10.2% in 2025, with about 34.5 million Americans still living below the official poverty line. Trump’s broader claim needs some context. The 2025 official poverty rate was historically low, and the child poverty rate reached a record low of 13.4%, according to the Census Bureau. However, the Supplemental Poverty Measure, which accounts for taxes, government benefits, housing costs and certain other expenses, stood at 13.1% in 2025 and was not statistically different from 2024. So the latest data show a meaningful decline in the official poverty rate, while different measures of economic hardship tell a more complicated story than the phrase “best poverty numbers ever” suggests. #democrats #uspolitics #whitehouse #corruption #poverty
